header.title: Rising memory and CPU costs squeeze notebook brands' margins and shipments in 2027

s01_bottom_line.text: TrendForce projects global notebook shipments to decline low-single-digit in 2027, worsening to high-single-digit if elevated DRAM/CPU costs are passed to consumers, with core components at ~68% of a US$900 notebook's BOM. ⟨cited figures: forecast; approximate⟩
Notebook brands face a margin-versus-volume squeeze that could pressure earnings, though the article does not quantify any specific brand's earnings or margin impact.

items.text: If DRAM and CPU prices stay elevated and are passed to consumers, the full-year shipment decline could reach the high-single-digit range. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩
For a US$900 MSRP mainstream notebook, CPU, DRAM and SSD made up about 68% of BOM cost in 3Q26. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩
Global notebook shipments are projected to decline by a low-single-digit percentage in 2027. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩
DRAM supply is likely to stay tight in 2027 as AI servers absorb capacity, with PC DRAM facing limited supply growth.
The primary 2027 notebook market risk is expected to shift from supply constraints to rising costs hurting demand.
Brands face a trade-off: raising prices weakens demand, absorbing costs squeezes gross margins.
